title: Generative AI Is Everywhere—Including At Birchwood Foods
text:
You may think that AI, and generative AI in particular, is an exotic species still primarily found in Silicon Valley. You may also have read that relatively few companies—my surveys say about 5 or 6%—have put generative AI use cases into production. However, there is certainly evidence to the contrary of these assertions.
Exhibit A is Birchwood Foods, a family-owned meat packing business based in Kenosha, Wisconsin. Neither that industry nor that location are generally at the forefront of AI usage, but Birchwood has a production application of AI that is likely to be saving its workers’ lives, or at least their extremities.
In recent years the US meatpacking industry (Birchwood isn’t a slaughter house but processes and packages meats) has become an occupational haven for an ethnically and geographically diverse workforce. Birchwood’s 1000 employees come from lots of different countries in Latin America, Asia, and Africa. That means that they often speak languages other than English. Do you speak Tigrynya? Wolof? Hakha Chin? Birchwood employees do. That makes it somewhat difficult to communicate important information to them. It’s particularly difficult when some employees are not literate even in their native languages.
AI for Health and Safety
Birchwood has historically used short videos to communicate safety and health-related information to its employees. This is generally an effective medium for learning, but only if the audience understands the language within the video. It was way too labor-intensive (and infeasible for English-only speakers) to record videos in every language that Birchwood employees speak, so Birchwood had previously used subtitles from a language translation company. That made the videos very expensive to produce, and many employees couldn’t read the captions.
In early 2023 Caitlin Hamstra, the Corporate Learning and Development Manager, mentioned to her boss that there might be a new solution to this problem based on recent AI developments. Kim Crawford, Birchwood’s head of HR, Safety, and Learning & Development, encouraged Hamstra to survey new technologies for translations in video-based learning. After experimenting with several different generative AI language models and vendors, Hamstra came across a UK-based startup called Synthesia. It specializes in creating avatar-based videos from text that can speak in multiple languages—131 of them at last count. Birchwood entered into a purchase agreement with Synthesia in October of 2023, and Hamstra and L&D Supervisor James Nolan began to implement their software.
Semi-Automated Translation for Safety Videos
Since that time, Birchwood has been very productive with AI-enabled translation. It has created 120 videos, each 5 or 6 minutes in length. They use avatars to do the speaking parts, and the 131 available languages cover 95% of the languages spoken at the plants. Crawford says that giving employees work instructions in their own language has led to very positive reactions. It helps, she says, with engagement, retention, safety, and buy-in to the job.
Each video typically highlights important steps that drive the particular work task, how Birchwood performs the work, and why it is performed that way. It’s also possible to create a presentation on a particular issue that is generated by a stakeholder in a plant. He or she can use the AI assistant with some slides, pick a tone, audience, and attitude, and create a video within a couple of minutes. Some stock courses that had previously been created at Birchwood, e.g. on water conservation, have been translated into new languages.
Birchwood can use the technology to rapidly create new content. For example, one evening there were some minor but worrisome injuries in a warehouse involving a forklift and a truck. The next morning, Birchwood was able to quickly create a new 5-minute video in the languages used by forklift drivers. The new videos are then deployed on tablets to supervisors, who ensure that the relevant employees see them quickly.
For all the videos, Nolan explained that Birchwood attempts to ensure that the translations are accurate. After the Synthesia software has created the translation, he said, Birchwood calls in the best available human translator to validate the quality of the language. If the translation isn’t accurate in some respect, they can make edits to it on the spot. They can also edit the avatar’s actions in explaining the topic. Crawford commented, “We don’t expect perfection; we just want to reach as many employees as possible.”
Generative AI and Better Video Communications
Since Birchwood began working with Synthesia, the vendor has used generative AI technology to create more than 20 new avatars with more lifelike motions. A recent article suggests that Synthesia is increasingly able to create lifelike avatars based on real people—what some might call “deepfakes,” but Synthesia prefers to call “synthetic media.” That would mean that various stakeholders at customers like Birchwood—including the CEO—could introduce and narrate videos and appear to speak them in many different languages.
Although many observers are justifiable concerned about AI’s potential negative impact on communications media, it’s important to remember the positive attributes of the technology. With tools like Synthesia and with generative AI more broadly, communications barriers due to language are sure to continue to fall. It may be that the concept of “foreign language” itself becomes foreign in the future.

title: How AI-First Companies Are Outpacing Rivals And Redefining The Future Of Work
text:
Generative AI is poised to redefine the future of work by enabling entirely new opportunities for operational efficiency and business model innovation. A recent Deloitte study found 43% of CEOs have already implemented genAI in their organizations to drive innovation and enhance their daily work but genAI’s business impact is just beginning. GenAI’s ability to generate content, automate tasks, and analyze information will require organizations to rethink digital transformation, moving from a technology-centric approach to one that focuses on reimagined business transformation.
AI’s potential to drive business transformation offers an unprecedented opportunity. As such, the CEOs most important role right now is to develop and articulate a clear vision for AI to enhance, automate, and augment work while simultaneously investing in value creation and innovation. Organizations need a bold, innovative vision for the future of work, or they risk falling behind as competitors mature exponentially, setting the stage for future, self-inflicted disruption.
To understand where we are and what organizations should be doing, we need to look beyond the sheer number of companies that are investing in artificial intelligence. Instead, we need to look deeper at how and why businesses are investing in AI, to what end, and how they are progressing and maturing over time. Tracking evolution and maturity at a peer level is necessary to understand learnings, best practices, and benchmarks which can help guide organizations on their business transformation journey.
AI Maturity Becomes the Benchmark to Guide AI-Led Business Transformation
How can we track and measure AI maturity? Over the last year, I had the opportunity to research and develop a foundational genAI business transformation maturity model in our ServiceNow Innovation Office. This model assessed foundational patterns and progress across five stages of maturity. This internal work was used as a guiding light for new research on AI maturity conducted by ServiceNow in partnership with Oxford economics.
The study looked at 4,500 businesses in 21 countries across eight industries using a proprietary index to measure AI maturity using a score from 0 to 100. ServiceNow’s research with Oxford Economics culminated in the newly released Enterprise AI Maturity Index, which found the average AI maturity score was 44 out of 100. The highest score was 71. Only one-in-six companies scored higher than 50.
In the report, ServiceNow found that, for most companies, AI-powered business transformation is in its infancy with 81% of companies planning to increase AI spending next year. But a select group of elite companies, identified as “Pacesetters,” are already pulling away from the pack. These Pacesetters are further advanced in their AI journeyand already successfully investing in AI innovation to create new business value.
The Enterprise AI Maturity Index suggests the vast majority of organizations are still in the early stages of AI maturity, while a select group of Pacesetters can offer us lessons for how to advance AI business transformation.
AI Pacesetters are Setting the Pace and Reaping the Rewards
The research published by ServiceNow and Oxford Economics found that Pacesetters are already accelerating investments in AI transformation. Specifically, these elite companies are exploring ways to break down silos to connect workflows, work, and data across disparate functions. These organizations are also cultivating the right skills for next-level work. What also sets Pacesetters apart is active C-suite leadership and involvement. For example, Pacesetters are operating with 2x C-suite vision (65% vs. 31% of others), engagement (64% vs. 33%), and clear measures of AI success (62% vs. 28%).
These elite companies are already realizing positive ROI, with one-in-three seeing ROI of 15% or more. Furthermore, 94% are increasing AI investments with 40% of Pacesetters boosting those investments by 15% or more.
AI Pacesetters are Optimizing Operations
Working smart and smarter is at the top of the list for companies seeking to optimize operations. Pacesetters are more likely than others to deploy AI for data cleaning, management, integration, and visualization (76% vs. 42%), performance management (68% vs. 36%), case summarization (60% vs. 40%), and predictive analytics (60% vs. 37%).
Another finding near and dear to me personally, is that Pacesetters are also using AI to improve customer experience. These companies are setting three-year investment priorities that include harnessing genAI to create customer support summaries and power customer agent assistants.
Elite Companies are Using AI to Rethink Work
For decades, leaders have explored how to break down silos to create a more connected enterprise. This is now mandatory for AI-powered business transformation. Connecting silos is how data becomes integrated, which fuels organizational intelligence and growth.
The ServiceNow and Oxford Economics research found that 60% of Pacesetters are making noteworthy progress toward breaking down data and operational silos. In fact, Pacesetting companies are more than four times as likely (54% vs. 12%) to invest in new ways of working designed from scratch, with human-AI collaboration baked-in from the onset. This approach helps organizations execute beyond business-as-usual automation to unlock innovative efficiency gains and value creation.
AI Pacesetters are Investing in Skills Assessments and Up-Skilling
When status quo companies use AI to automate existing work, they often fall into the trap of prioritizing cost-cutting. Pacesetters prioritize growth opportunities via augmentation, which unlocks new capabilities and competitiveness. For example, elite companies prepare people for AI transformation, with 61% of Pacesetters compared to just 30% of other organizations in the study reporting that they already possess the right mix of skills and experience to execute against C-suite vision and strategy.
To help people learn, unlearn, and grow, leaders need to empower employees and surround them with a sense of safety, resources, and leadership to move in new directions. This is what it means to create a culture of innovation. It’s giving employees a future motivating state (vision); reinforcing the day-to-day mission with relevant imagery and verbal support, training and rewards; and supportive policies and resources to establish new norms, behaviors, and standards. According to the report, two-thirds of Pacesetters allow teams to identify problems and recommend AI solutions autonomously. And almost 70% empower employees to make decisions about AI solutions to solve specific functional business needs.
To fortify growth along the stages of AI maturity, Pacesetters are identifying new roles needed to thrive in a new future of work. These companies are seeking to fill the following roles through hiring or upskilling:
- AI configurators
- Data scientists
- Experience developers
- Machine learning engineers
More mature organizations are also investing in innovation cultures to promote upskilling and AI fluency. Pacesetters are more likely than others to have implemented training and support programs to identify AI champions, evangelize the technology from the bottom up, and to host learning events across the organization. On the other hand, for non-Pacesetter companies, just 44% are implementing even one of these steps.
AI Governance Defines the Rules to Guide Exploration and Experimentation
The best companies in any era of transformation stand-up a center of excellence (CoE). The goal is to bring together experts and cross-functional teams to drive initiatives and establish best practices. CoEs also play an important role in mitigating risks, managing data quality, and ensuring workforce transformation. AI CoEs are also tasked with responsible AI usage while minimizing potential harm.
Pacesetters report that the top five AI risks and challenges they’re managing include:
- Cybersecurity
- Regulatory compliance
- Personal/Individual privacy
- Intellectual-property infringement
- Workforce/Labor displacement
Without data, there can be no intelligence. Data governance also plays an important role in AI CoEs. Pacesetters are making significant headway over their peers by acquiring technologies and establishing new processes to integrate and optimize data (63% vs. 43%). These companies also have formalized data governance and privacy compliance (62% vs 44%). Pacesetter leaders are also proactive, meeting new AI governance needs and creating AI-specific policies to protect sensitive data and maintain regulatory compliance (59% vs. 42%).
Pacesetters prioritize critical aspects of data governance as follows:
- Assessed AI apps and data requirements
- Formalized data compliance
- Resources to integrate and optimize data
- Mapped structured and unstructured data
- Addressed evolving data governance and security
- Connected data and operational silos
As AI continues to evolve, so will the need to continuously explore and experiment. Innovation becomes necessary as its own function, guided by the AI CoE.
Pacesetters report that in addition to standing-up AI Centers of Excellence (62% vs. 41%), they lead the pack by establishing innovation centers to test new AI tools and solutions (62% vs. 39%).
Successful innovation centers also foster an ecosystem for collaboration and co-innovation. Working with external AI experts can provide additional expertise and resources to explore new AI solutions and keep up with AI advancements.
Measure for AI Iteration and Innovation
Leading organizations must consider AI strategy investments on two fronts 1) iteration (optimizing existing business and operational models) and 2) innovation (creating value through new business and operational models).
Ninety-four percent of Pacesetter organizations report that they will increase AI spending in the year ahead. Unlike less mature organizations, elites spend time up front defining the business value and outcomes they seek.
There’s a saying, what gets measured gets managed and actioned. William Bruce Cameron also famously said, “Not everything that can be counted counts, and not everything that counts can be counted.”
AI is revealing uncharted paths toward a new future of work. Progress toward unknown fronts requires direction and measures to chart momentum. It’s critical to put in place measures that assess progress against AI vision and strategy. Yet only 35% of organizations say that have defined clear metrics to measure the impact of AI investments.
Leading Organizations Measure ROI Against C-Suite Vision and Strategy
ServiceNow and Oxford Economics learned that more than three-quarters of organizations surveyed focused AI returns on increased productivity, enhanced customer experience, higher revenue, improved competitive positioning, and faster innovation. For example, 74% of Pacesetters report AI investments are achieving positive returns in the form of accelerated innovation.
Across the board, Pacesetters are achieving 15%+ AI ROI across the following business outcomes:
- Risk management
- Improved competitive positioning
- Cost reduction
- Revenue growth
- Improved employee experience
- Improved customer experience
- Ability to innovate faster
- Increased efficiency productivity
Looking ahead, Pacesetters are prioritizing AI investments to achieve the following operational and business outcomes:
- Increased efficiency/productivity
- Improved customer experience
- Revenue growth
- Improved competitive positioning growth
- Ability to innovate faster
- Cost reduction
- Risk management
- Improved employee experience
AI Offers Leaders a Unique Opportunity to Reimagine the Future of Work
AI-powered business transformation is still in its early days. AI will only continue to transform how companies operate, go to market, and compete.
AI maturity represents a moment in time. AI-powered business transformation will play out over the longer-term, with key decisions required at every step and every level. Even today, we are still early in realizing and defining the potential of the future of work. The future still requires its dreamers and architects.
To achieve AI excellence and accelerate business transformation, apply the following lessons learned from today’s Pacesetters:
Engage Leadership in AI Integration:
- Senior executives should lead AI implementation and ensure it aligns with strategic goals.
- Leaders drive transformation from the top because executive involvement is crucial for successful AI integration and achieving high maturity in AI capabilities.
Establish Governance for AI:
- Develop and enforce governance policies to prevent AI from accessing restricted data or making unauthorized decisions.
- Implement checks and balances to ensure AI insights are used responsibly and do not lead to harmful consequences.
Connect People, Data, and Processes Using AI:
- Implement AI to streamline and integrate data flows across various functions such as payroll, procurement, employee requests, customer queries, and content creation.
- Ensure AI systems support and accelerate routine tasks, enhancing overall efficiency and effectiveness throughout the enterprise.
Scale Process Improvements with AI:
- Adopt an enterprise AI platform to facilitate collaborative efforts and streamline processes.
- Integrate AI across customer service, technical support, and customer interactions to speed up responses and allow employees to focus on more strategic tasks.
As companies scramble for AI maturity, composure, vision, and execution become key. Pacesetters may have the early lead, but the race has just begun. This is the time to make your move.

title: Council Post: The Future Of Learning Operations: Embracing Predictive Analytics And AI
text:
Ryan Austin is Founder and CEO of Cognota. You can attend free virtual workshops to learn how to run L&D like a business.
In today's fast-changing business landscape, Learning and Development (L&D) is more critical than ever, with workforce development and reskilling becoming strategic priorities for staying competitive.
Recently, a group of Chief Learning Officers (CLOs) formed the CLO Lift initiative to tackle L&D challenges. Their collaborative efforts produced articles on learning governance, emphasizing the importance of creating internal learning advisory boards. (You can see them speak at the Virtual LearnOps Summit on September 25.)
While pivotal, learning operations are set for transformation through predictive analytics and AI. Having taught and spoken on learning governance at workshops like "Reinventing Learning Operations" with CLOs Rob Lauber and Martha Soehren, I've reflected on how these technologies can revolutionize time-consuming strategies like building and managing learning advisory boards.
The Current State: Governance And Advisory Boards
The CLO Lift initiative's focus on governance highlights L&D as a strategic function. Governance structures and learning advisory boards ensure learning initiatives align with organizational goals by providing insights into departmental talent needs and fostering collaboration.
These governance models help prioritize learning investments for maximum returns and create a framework for continuous improvement through feedback and after-action reviews. This approach has aligned L&D with business priorities, leading to measurable improvements in employee skills and organizational performance.
The Future State: Predictive Analytics And AI
While governance and advisory boards have laid a solid foundation, the future of learning operations lies in harnessing the power of predictive analytics and AI. These technologies offer unprecedented opportunities to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of L&D strategies, transforming how we approach workforce development.
Predictive Analytics: Anticipating Learning Needs
Predictive analytics uses historical data and statistical algorithms to forecast future outcomes. In L&D, it can anticipate learning needs by analyzing employee performance, skills gaps and industry trends. This proactive approach addresses skills deficiencies before they become critical, ensuring the workforce is prepared for emerging challenges.
For example, predictive analytics identifies employees at risk of missing performance targets due to skills gaps, allowing tailored learning interventions to improve performance and reduce turnover. Additionally, predictive models can forecast the impact of new technologies and market changes on skill requirements, helping organizations stay competitive.
A Solid Predictive Training Request Process: A Game Changer Vs. Common Learning Advisory Boards
One transformative application of predictive analytics in L&D is the training request process. Historically, L&D teams have been viewed as order takers, responding to "intakes" rather than consulting strategically. I've advocated for shifting from "intakes" to "requests," allowing L&D to take a more proactive approach. Requests enable L&D to assess actual needs and prioritize investments.
My perspective has evolved to recognize the value of both requests and intakes in a comprehensive L&D strategy. In my last article, I discussed integrating top-down and bottom-up approaches. Building on this, incorporating a company-wide training intake process can be beneficial, despite concerns about manageability if every employee can submit a request.
This is where predictive analytics and AI come into play. These technologies can streamline the management of requests, allowing AI to review, analyze patterns and prioritize them based on corporate objectives. Predictive analytics can recommend which requests L&D should focus on, ensuring resources are allocated effectively.
To implement this strategy successfully, L&D must align with the organization's top priorities and goals. Without this alignment, the strategy fails. However, the benefits are significant, enabling L&D to identify overlooked training needs that align with corporate objectives.
Furthermore, integrating the intake process with financial budget planning and procurement systems can reveal spending redundancies and vendor overlaps, optimizing tail spend. This ensures every dollar invested in L&D is used efficiently and effectively.
Steps To Building An Effective Intake Strategy
1. Define objectives and align with corporate goals: Clearly define the objectives of your intake process and align them with the organization's strategic priorities to gain executive support and position L&D as a strategic partner.
2. Develop a robust data collection system: Avoid using basic forms like Google or Microsoft Forms, email or spreadsheets. Instead, invest in a robust LearnOps platform to capture underlying data such as which departments or employees are submitting requests.
3. Implement AI and predictive analytics: Use AI to review and categorize incoming requests, analyzing patterns to prioritize based on strategic priorities. Predictive analytics can forecast the impact of requests, offering data-driven recommendations.
4. Build a workflow for routing requests: Develop a workflow that routes prioritized requests to the appropriate L&D teams for consultations or action, ensuring high-priority requests are promptly addressed by the right people.
5. Integrate with financial and procurement systems: Link your intake process with financial and procurement systems to gain insights into spending patterns, identify redundancies, optimize tail spend and demonstrate that L&D is a strategic advisor, not just a cost center.
The Shift From Time-Consuming To Efficient Strategies
Integrating predictive analytics and AI into learning operations shifts from time-consuming, manual processes to efficient, data-driven strategies. Traditionally, building and managing learning advisory boards required significant time and effort. Predictive analytics and AI can streamline these tasks, providing real-time insights and automating routines.
This shift enhances efficiency and improves decision-making. Leveraging data and AI allows organizations to make informed decisions about learning investments, ensuring resources are allocated to the most impactful initiatives.
Conclusion: Embracing The Future Of LearnOps
Predictive analytics and AI will likely transform the future of learning operations by anticipating learning needs and streamlining tasks, driving efficiency and effectiveness in L&D strategies.
While the insights from the CLO Lift initiative and the focus on learning governance remain relevant, integrating predictive analytics and AI is the next evolution in learning operations. These advancements enable agile, data-driven learning ecosystems that support continuous improvement and strategic alignment with business goals.
As someone deeply involved in evolving learning operations, I am excited about the possibilities these technologies bring. By leveraging them, we can move beyond traditional methods to create scalable, predictable and easily managed learning governance, driving impactful L&D outcomes.

title: Council Post: Harnessing Technology In A Phygital World
text:
Alonso Vargas, SVP of Product at Flybuy.
Imagine walking into a store and instantly getting personalized recommendations on your phone based on your online browsing history, or ordering dinner through an app, and when you arrive at the restaurant, your food is ready, tailored perfectly to your tastes and dietary preferences down to the tomato on the side with extra dressing.
This is the essence of the "phygital" experience—a seamless blend of physical and digital interactions, where online interactions set the stage to enhance real-world experiences. It’s not just a glimpse into the future but a transformative shift in how businesses will engage with customers.
As consumers navigate a world that is bridging the physical and digital realms, businesses have a golden opportunity to increase engagement and loyalty by leveraging advanced technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) and location technology.
By harnessing the power of data and location intelligence, brands can offer a personalized, efficient and highly satisfying customer experience. This opens up a world of possibilities to delight and captivate, setting a new standard for customer satisfaction.
Challenges In Navigating The Phygital Landscape
In the post-Covid era, digital transformation has accelerated to meet customer expectations. The dominance of the digital ordering experience is becoming more prevalent in this evolving landscape, and industry leaders are highlighting this shift.
For instance, Yum Brands has experienced over 50% of their sales being placed digitally this year; Chipotle's digital sales hit $3.7 billion in 2023; and Wendy’s digital sales jumped 30% in 2023. In the retail sector, Walmart’s online retail reached the $100 billion mark—a 23% increase in global online sales for the second-largest e-commerce retailer in the U.S. market. In grocery, Kroger’s CEO says that "digital is an important growth accelerator in our business" after digital sales grew to reach $12 billion in 2023. These statistics emphasize the growing consumer preference for easy, personalized digital interactions.
Despite the apparent opportunities, many businesses are struggling to keep pace with these digital changes. The key problem is how to integrate advanced technology effectively and create personalized and engaging phygital experiences. Companies must navigate the complex consumer expectations and evolving technological advancements.
Leveraging AI And Location Technology For Phygital Success
In the phygital era, leveraging AI and location technology can create frictionless, personalized experiences to foster deeper loyalty and satisfaction during real-time interactions. AI is a critical tool in delivering these experiences because it can prioritize a consumer-centric approach while simultaneously running location technology to provide real-time updates and accurately time an order pickup or delivery.
To help deliver the best customer experience, here are four strategic ways to harness technology in today’s phygital world.
1. Implementing Personalized AI Solutions
Utilize AI to analyze consumer insights and create personalized experiences. AI-driven algorithms can tailor product recommendations based on a customer’s past purchases, online behavior and location data.
For example, Amazon uses advanced machine learning algorithms to recommend products to users based on their previous purchases and browsing history, significantly boosting customer satisfaction and driving sales (in fact, up to 35% of Amazon's total sales).
Similarly, Netflix employs a hybrid recommendation system, using user-based and item-based collaborative filtering alongside content-based methods to suggest new content based on similarities between users' viewing histories and the attributes of the content itself. This provides highly personalized content recommendations, helping retain subscribers and increase viewing times.
Knowing a customer's frequent location allows for hyper-targeted recommendations and promotions that are relevant to their lifestyle and preferences, enhancing customer satisfaction and increasing repeat business.
2. Enhancing Real-Time Engagement
Deliver messaging at the exact time a customer may make a purchasing decision using advanced location technology. By providing offers and updates when they are most relevant to the consumer’s current location and activity, such as sending a notification to loyalty members when they are near a store, businesses can maintain consumer interest and drive engagement, effectively bridging the gap between online browsing and in-store experiences.
3. Optimizing Omnichannel Strategies
Develop a smart omnichannel strategy that leverages the customer’s location and AI to provide a seamless customer experience across all touchpoints. AI ensures personalized service across all channels, recognizing consumer preferences across various shopping methods.
For example, Starbucks uses AI to provide personalized drink recommendations based on past purchases, location data and even time of day. This allows customers to receive suggestions tailored to their preferences, whether they are ordering via the app, in-store or at a drive-thru. This AI-driven approach has significantly increased customer engagement and loyalty, evidenced by the growth of the Starbucks Rewards program.
Additionally, location technology guides in-store navigation and syncs online carts with in-store availability, blending digital and physical interactions.
4. Utilizing Data Analytics For Insights
AI-powered data analytics can uncover valuable insights into consumer behavior by integrating location data, enabling businesses to anticipate trends and adapt their strategies accordingly. By analyzing patterns and predicting future behaviors based on location and activity, companies can stay ahead of the curve and meet evolving consumer demands. For example, understanding peak shopping times and popular locations helps businesses optimize staffing and inventory management.
Embracing The Phygital Future
As we move further into the phygital era, businesses should recognize that consumers' perceptions are shaped by both in-person experiences and digital interactions. The journey toward a phygital consumer experience involves reimagining the consumer's reality in a dynamic and unique way.
I believe the integration of AI and new technology is not just a competitive advantage but a necessity. By staying abreast of the latest trends and harnessing the power of digital technologies, businesses can continue to navigate the post-Covid world with confidence and success. The future is phygital, and AI can help unlock its full potential.
